The log of a result or a session

Source: R/log_render.R
sas_log.Rd

The log as plain text, as text coloured for the terminal, or as HTML.

Usage

sas_log(
  x,
  format = c("plain", "ansi", "html"),
  echo = log_echo_default,
  ...,
  compact = FALSE,
  session
)

Arguments

x

A result of sas_run() or a session from sas_session().

format

"plain", "ansi" or "html".

echo

Show the program lines (TRUE, the default) or only the messages and PUT output (FALSE).

...

Not used; the arguments after it are given by name.

compact

The compact layout of the echo (TRUE) or the default layout with the line numbers in 11 columns (FALSE, the default).

session

The former name of x (a session), still accepted; with session, x is left out (or is the format, given by position).

Value

"plain" and "ansi": a character vector of class sasonr_log, one element per line; it prints as the log text, one line per element. as.character() gives the plain character vector; [ keeps the class. "html": a character string.

Details

  • "plain": the SAS-style log text, one element per line: the lines of x$log (for a session: the log of all submissions).

  • "ansi": the same lines coloured with cli (ERROR red, WARNING green, NOTE blue, PUT output unstyled), under a summary line that counts the ERROR and WARNING lines of the messages (PUT output that starts with ERROR: is not counted). print() of a result uses this view in a terminal with colours; options(sasonr.log_style = "plain") turns it off.

  • "html": one string, a <div class="sas-log"> with a <details> block per step and the lines in <span> elements of the classes sas-note, sas-warning, sas-error, sas-put and sas-src (source lines). The style sheet is system.file("css", "sasonr.css", package = "sasonr"); the HTML has no inline styles.

Every view shows the program lines with their line numbers (echo = FALSE: the messages and PUT output only): each line with its number left-justified in 11 columns, a line longer than LINESIZE continued on lines that start with !; a compile-time ERROR right after its line, with an underscore marker and the error number under the line when the column is known; a blank line after a numbered ERROR message (ERROR 22-322: ..., except in PROC MEANS, SUMMARY, UNIVARIATE, TRANSPOSE, COMPARE, SORT, FREQ, RANK, APPEND and CONTENTS when more of the step's lines follow); a blank line between a step's lines and what the step writes when it runs (when the step ends on the line of its numbered ERRORs, this blank line comes before them and each of them is followed by a blank line). The data lines after DATALINES / CARDS are not echoed. The program's OPTIONS SOURCE and OPTIONS NOSOURCE turn the echo on and off.

Limits of the echo: it shows the lines of the program as written, numbered from 1 in each submission (a session does not continue the numbering); code generated by macros (MPRINT lines) and %INCLUDE lines are not shown; the NOTEs written while a step is compiled follow the step's lines; the statements of a PROC SQL step that share a line are not split onto ! lines; a line on which RUN; is followed by more text is echoed whole (in SAS the rest follows the step's messages); lines with multibyte characters wrap by characters; the timing NOTEs of SAS are not written. When the echo cannot be shown exactly, the echo of that submission is left out and the log starts with a NOTE that says why; the run itself goes on: a numbered ERROR on a line with a macro reference (a macro variable, call, statement or comment), a compile-time ERROR on a line that OPTIONS NOSOURCE hides, OPTIONS SOURCE / NOSOURCE with more text on its line, a numbered WARNING. For now a NOTE place ((Line):(Column), at line N column M) on a line with a macro reference fails loud.

compact = TRUE is a narrower layout of the echo for display: the line number takes as many columns as the largest line number of the view needs, plus one blank; a continuation line starts with ! in those columns. The lines break where they do in the default layout, and the underscore markers and error numbers under a line move with its text. The messages are unchanged (the places in a NOTE are program lines and columns).

See also

The events behind every view are the log_events field of a result (a tibble: seq, submission, step, phase, kind, id, args, at, places, text, source_line).

Examples

res <- sas_run("data a;\n  x = 1;\n  put x=;\nrun;")
sas_log(res)
#> 1          data a;
#> 2            x = 1;
#> 3            put x=;
#> 4          run;
#> 
#> x=1
#> NOTE: The data set WORK.A has 1 observations and 1 variables.
sas_log(res, echo = FALSE)
#> x=1
#> NOTE: The data set WORK.A has 1 observations and 1 variables.
sas_log(res, compact = TRUE)
#> 1 data a;
#> 2   x = 1;
#> 3   put x=;
#> 4 run;
#> 
#> x=1
#> NOTE: The data set WORK.A has 1 observations and 1 variables.
cat(sas_log(res, "html"))
#> <div class="sas-log">
#> <p class="sas-log-summary">No ERRORs or WARNINGs</p>
#> <details class="sas-step" open><summary>DATA step (line 1)</summary>
#> <pre class="sas-log-text"><span class="sas-src">1          data a;</span>
#> <span class="sas-src">2            x = 1;</span>
#> <span class="sas-src">3            put x=;</span>
#> <span class="sas-src">4          run;</span>
#> <span class="sas-src"></span>
#> <span class="sas-put">x=1</span>
#> <span class="sas-note">NOTE: The data set WORK.A has 1 observations and 1 variables.</span></pre>
#> </details>
#> </div>
res$log_events[, c("step", "kind", "id")]
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>    step kind  id        
#>   <int> <chr> <chr>     
#> 1     1 echo  raw       
#> 2     1 put   raw       
#> 3     1 note  ds.created
